original_value: This paper focuses on evaluating the ability and contribution of using backscatter intensity, texture, coherence, and color features extracted from Sentinel-1A data for urban land cover classification and comparing different multi-sensor land cover mapping methods to improve classification accuracy. Both Landsat-8 OLI and Hyperion images were also acquired, in combination with Sentinel-1A data, to explore the potential of different multi-sensor urban land cover mapping methods to improve classification accuracy. The classification was performed using a random forest (RF) method. The results showed that the optimal window size of the combination of all texture features was 9 × 9, and the optimal window size was different for each individual texture feature. For the four different feature types, the texture features contributed the most to the classification, followed by the coherence and backscatter intensity features; and the color features had the least impact on the urban land cover classification. Satisfactory classification results can be obtained using only the combination of texture and coherence features, with an overall accuracy up to 91.55% and a kappa coefficient up to 0.8935, respectively. Among all combinations of Sentinel-1A-derived features, the combination of the four features had the best classification result. Multi-sensor urban land cover mapping obtained higher classification accuracy. The combination of Sentinel-1A and Hyperion data achieved higher classification accuracy compared to the combination of Sentinel-1A and Landsat-8 OLI images, with an overall accuracy of up to 99.12% and a kappa coefficient up to 0.9889. When Sentinel-1A data was added to Hyperion images, the overall accuracy and kappa coefficient were increased by 4.01% and 0.0519, respectively.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines how backscatter intensity, texture, coherence, and color features derived from Sentinel-1A data contribute to urban land cover classification, and compares different multi-sensor mapping approaches for improving classification accuracy. It also acquired Landsat-8 OLI and Hyperion imagery alongside Sentinel-1A data to investigate the potential of multi-sensor urban land cover mapping methods for boosting accuracy. Classification was carried out with a random forest (RF) method. Results indicated that the best window size for the full set of texture features was 9 × 9, while the optimal window size varied for each individual texture feature. Across the four feature types, texture features had the greatest impact on classification, followed by coherence and backscatter intensity, whereas color features contributed the least. Reasonably good classification results were achieved using only texture and coherence features, with overall accuracy reaching 91.55% and a kappa coefficient reaching 0.8935. Among all Sentinel-1A-derived feature combinations, using all four features together produced the best classification performance. Multi-sensor urban land cover mapping achieved higher classification accuracy. The combination of Sentinel-1A and Hyperion data outperformed Sentinel-1A plus Landsat-8 OLI images, reaching an overall accuracy of up to 99.12% and a kappa coefficient up to 0.9889. Adding Sentinel-1A data to Hyperion imagery increased overall accuracy and the kappa coefficient by 4.01% and 0.0519, respectively.
